name: The Civilizational Risks of a UAP Technology Arms Race: Nonhuman Technology and Global Security
summary: Policy paper by Marik von Rennenkampff examining the global-security risks that could arise if states were competing to exploit advanced technology of alleged nonhuman origin. The paper treats such an arms race as a consequential policy scenario and argues for international cooperation and control mechanisms; it does not itself establish that any government possesses nonhuman technology.
eventCategory: UAP policy and global security publication

relationships.context: Marik von Rennenkampff authored this Sol Foundation policy paper.
Published by The Sol Foundation as Policy Papers, Vol. 2, No. 3.
Analyzes strategic instability, secrecy and global-security risks under a hypothetical UAP technology arms-race scenario.
Examines policy consequences arising from claims or scenarios involving technology of alleged nonhuman origin without treating those claims as established fact.
Discusses allegations and strategic implications of efforts to exploit or reverse engineer advanced UAP-associated technology.
Considers how public acknowledgment or disclosure could alter geopolitical competition and international security.
